synopsis: The booklet implements the reusable holdout principle by limiting the tuning team's access to aggregate pass/fail results from the audit set [f6955, f14333]. The glossary specifies that this restriction applies at release gates [f14291]. Chapter 9 and the glossary attribute the principle to adaptive data analysis work by Dwork and colleagues published in Science in 2015 [f6955, f14291]. The supplied facts agree on the access restriction but do not describe how aggregation is performed or what safeguards accompany repeated use [f6955, f14333, f14291].

relations.note: Both define implementation through restricting tuning-team access to aggregate pass/fail results.
Both describe aggregate-only access and cite Dwork's 2015 Science work.
Both state the access restriction; the latter specifies release gates and attribution.
